Windows archive-path worker, retail 0x597d00: no corresponding function in the complete DC procedure/declaration corpus. LoadAnimHeaders and LoadSoundHeaders call this separate std::string-returning function. It copies the drive-letter global, appends 25 encoded bytes, XORs their indexed positions and returns the resulting path. The Windows drive/archive consumers establish smackmgr ownership; the descriptive name is provisional, without claiming the DC media stubs define this operation.

ShowVideo calls it for both tracks. The explicit Win32 file-handle/Smacker operation is separate from DC VideoOpen, whose existing counterpart remains intact.

column4: Windows Smacker playback setup, retail 0x598af0: no corresponding procedure/declaration in DC. Separate eight-int fastcall body, ret 24, is called by the retained VideoPlay/VideoOpen wrappers. It closes old playback, selects track/no-skip/pixel flags, calls 0x598790 for audio and picture tracks, sets dimensions and invokes imported SmackVolumePan/SmackToBuffer. DC retains platform video stubs and NextSmackerFrame/CloseSmacker, but no body or declaration for this setup worker.

Its retained 37-byte body tests video pointer, ready flag and pause state before imported SmackDoFrame 0x63a454. CGameTransferSmack::SetPercentage invokes it separately from frame advancement. DC VideoDrawCurrentFrame is the older public wrapper, not this distinct namespace helper.

Windows Smacker seek worker, retail 0x5990a0: no matching namespace procedure/declaration in DC. Separate one-frame fastcall body checks video pointer and readiness, then calls imported SmackGoto 0x63a45c. The transfer-progress caller uses it with DrawSmackerFrame; it is distinct from DC NextSmackerFrame and VideoRestart and remains with the Windows Smacker backend.

Complete spell-selection worker, retail 0x59f700: no matching free procedure/declaration in DC. Retained one-hex fastcall body is shared by three target-selection call sites. It reads next-action/spell/mastery, validates the grid/target (0x5a39c0), updates mouse pointer and target/failure text, and applies area/highlighter state. The creature-spell action path and shared retained body distinguish it from the older manager GetSpellTarget/WindowHandler callers. Its static linkage and descriptive name remain provisional.

Complete creature missile helper, retail 0x59fde0: no corresponding x/y/army member in the full DC combatManager corpus. army::animate_missile calls this retained ret-12 member. It tests IsQuickCombat 0x46a4a0, obtains target MidY/MidX, then calls ShootAnimatedMissile 0x467db0 with the magic-arrow angle/sprite pair and count five. Existing generic missile methods retain their own identities; ordinal spelling is provisional.

Complete loss-recording wrapper, retail 0x5f2e10: no corresponding member in the full DC class field list/procedure corpus. The older predicate has its own matching body; this new wrapper records the successful result.

The one-message fastcall body checks click/right-modifier, selects origin z=0, updates both level buttons and redraws map/radar/screen. DC TViewWorldWindow has only rollover/origin/view dimensions and its older WindowHandler; the added button members and address-taken callback prove the new interface.

Separate one-message fastcall body selects origin z=1, reverses the surface/underground button states and redraws map/radar/screen. Its distinct address and level value establish the second callback, alongside the retained older WindowHandler.

Windows DirectDraw recovery, retail 0x6003c0: no corresponding function in DC. DDBlit calls this separate RECT-pointer helper on wrong-mode retry paths. It changes cooperative level/display mode, restores or recreates the primary surface and clipper, and updates window coordinates/style and preferences. All HRESULT failures pass the embedded C:\Dev\Heroes 3 Exp 2\Game\WINGRAPH.CPP string at 0x68c87c to ddsd, proving Windows source ownership independently of the provisional helper name.

That retained town reader (0x5bcd60) returns ret 8 and uses the version for saved hero IDs and legacy town names. The canonical helper keeps the count/resize/town-load sequence from DC.
